releases.title: Cloudflare-first runtime
changes: Cut over recurring pickup, RATS and health checks from cron-job.org/GitHub Actions polling to Cloudflare Cron Triggers with private KV hot state.
Common Telegram read-only questions now stay on the Cloudflare fast path with structured deterministic intent handling, bounded Groq intent classification and short conversation context.

Cloudflare performs lightweight source change detection and dispatches GitHub pickup/league reconciliation only when data changes; GitHub remains responsible for CI, deployment, durable encrypted repository state, Calendar reconciliation and state-changing fallback commands.

Added notification-silent live source verification and KV priming before edge activation, stable webhook authentication, serialized Worker deployments and automatic cron-job.org fallback restoration if an edge deployment fails.
Moved watchdog health semantics from GitHub workflow freshness to Cloudflare KV/source heartbeats and hardened source fingerprints so failed reconciliation dispatches are retried.

releases.title: Cloudflare primary-runtime preview
changes: Added a Cloudflare scheduled edge runtime for 2-minute pickup checks, 5-minute RATS checks, and 10-minute health/deep-watchdog coordination.
Added private Cloudflare KV hot-state support for current soccer snapshots, conversation context, AI budget, fingerprints and scheduler health.
Edge polling dispatches the existing GitHub pickup/league workflows only when source data changes, moving routine GitHub Actions out of the normal polling hot path after cutover.
Added notification-silent shadow refresh verification before legacy cron-job.org schedules are disabled.
Added dynamic KV provisioning with a manual CLOUDFLARE_KV_NAMESPACE_ID fallback, plus Worker bundle and edge-runtime regression tests.
Activation remains gated until Cloudflare KV access is available; failed cutover verification leaves the existing cron-job.org production schedules active.

releases.title: Cloudflare fast path and AI intent routing
changes: Added a Cloudflare read-only fast path that answers common Telegram questions directly from encrypted GitHub state without starting a GitHub Actions runner.
Added short-lived conversation context so follow-up questions such as 'what field?', 'what time?' and 'how many?' can refer to the previously discussed pickup date.
Added Groq intent classification at the edge for natural-language read-only questions while keeping facts and actions deterministic.
Split the free AI budget into 25 edge classifications and 25 GitHub fallback calls per UTC day.
Stored private AI feature-request classification metadata for later improvement without publishing request text.

releases.title: Private feature requests
changes: Replaced public request text, IDs and timestamps with an allowlisted category/count summary; original requests remain encrypted.
Added request privacy regression tests, strict public-summary schema validation and a listener audit before state commits.
Preserved encrypted request archives on decryption failure and documented dedicated-key migration requirements.

releases.title: Direct-main maintenance and silent testing
changes: Allowed validated repository maintenance changes to commit directly to main again and removed the PR-only governance requirement.
Made the manual smoke test notification-silent: it verifies refreshed pickup and league data without sending Telegram messages or changing Google Calendar.
Removed default monitored team names from README while keeping the configured defaults in code.
Updated scheduled ChatGPT maintenance guidance to sync current repository instructions before changes and avoid Telegram notifications during testing.

releases.title: Manual data purge and protected main
changes: Added a manual Purge current data GitHub Action that clears generated pickup, league, Calendar-reconciliation, watchdog, and feature-request data while preserving configuration and secrets.
Added repository governance setup for a concise GitHub description and PR-only normal changes to main, with a narrow GitHub Actions bypass for encrypted runtime-state persistence.
Simplified README and agent guidance and required scheduled ChatGPT maintenance to sync from current main and use branch + pull request changes.

releases.title: Deleted Calendar event recovery
changes: Versioned league Calendar tracking keys so stale Apps Script event-ID mappings from manually deleted Calendar events are invalidated.
The Calendar bridge now falls back to matching an active event or creating a fresh event instead of reusing the previous tracking property.
Added regression coverage for the versioned Calendar tracking key.

releases.title: Concurrent state replay hardening
changes: Reworked workflow state persistence to replay generated encrypted state onto the latest main branch before each push attempt.
Prevents rebase conflicts from losing Calendar-applied league snapshots when listener, pickup, league, or watchdog workflows commit concurrently.

releases.title: Default league team bootstrap
changes: Added Third Touch FC and PhoSaiGon as built-in league defaults in that priority order for clean/fresh state.
Encrypted Telegram-managed league team state remains authoritative after bootstrap, so teams can still be added, removed, or renamed.
Purged previously retrieved pickup and league match snapshots before clean-bootstrap end-to-end testing.

releases.title: Calendar bridge deployment compatibility
changes: Updated the Apps Script deployment workflow to replace the Code.js filename produced by clasp pull, avoiding duplicate Code.js/Code.gs conflicts.
Verified the full Calendar bridge CI path: project pull, code push, existing deployment update, live webhook health check, and OAuth cleanup.

releases.title: One-time release announcements
changes: Replaced the single last-announcement marker with persisted announcement-ID history so each enabled release/feature announcement is delivered only once per stored bot state.
Historical announcements are marked seen during migration so older releases cannot rotate back into Telegram.
Cleared all currently stored public/redacted and encrypted/private feature suggestions.

releases.title: Concurrent state persistence hardening
changes: Added bounded pull/rebase/push retries to listener, pickup, league, and watchdog state persistence.
Prevents transient Git ref races between independently scheduled workflows from dropping otherwise successful runs.

releases.title: League team migration reliability
changes: Fixed legacy league-team migration so a valid legacy configuration replaces an existing empty encrypted placeholder.
Preserved the rule that only encrypted league-team state is persisted in BallerWatch.

releases.title: Operational setup runbooks
changes: Added an agent skill for safely discovering and verifying the pickup UPSTREAM_ENDPOINT without committing its live value.
Added repository agent guidance so future maintenance uses the endpoint-discovery procedure and preserves privacy.
Clarified that TRACKER_STATE_KEY is optional when the existing deployment uses the TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN encryption fallback.
Expanded the validation workflow triggers so version history and operational guidance changes are validated automatically.

releases.title: Versioned release history
changes: Added a SemVer release ledger with current version and chronological change history.
Telegram feature announcements now include the release version.
Added /version and version commands to report the current release and latest changes.
Scheduled ChatGPT maintenance tasks must record a release entry whenever they change the product.

releases.title: Automated infrastructure provisioning
changes: Added idempotent cron-job.org API provisioning for listener, pickup, league, and watchdog workflows.
Added automated Google Apps Script Calendar bridge deployment using the existing deployment ID.
Hardened privacy checks against committing Apps Script OAuth/config credentials.

releases.title: BallerWatch consolidated baseline
changes: Consolidated pickup, league, Telegram, Calendar, watchdog, privacy, and feature-builder automation into BallerWatch.
Kept live soccer data and user configuration encrypted at rest.
Added watchdog recovery, manual smoke testing, and privacy-redacted feature requests.
